breakdown_by_question_summary.pattern: FMD appears only in trust/process/low-pressure/word-of-mouth questions, and when it appears it ranks 1-3 with 100% sentiment. It is absent from every service-scope, seasonal, weather, family-mess, and pet-odor question — including 'kid messes, car seats, and snack stains' and 'dog hair and pet odors', the two questions that name FMD's own claimed specialty.

brand_strength_factors: Process transparency (47-point checklist, before/after photos, guarantees) that reduces anxiety and builds trust
Clear, flat pricing with photo-based quotes and minimal upsell pressure
Consistently strong results and 'almost like new' interior transformations
High trust and professionalism for mobile work at homes/offices (communication, punctuality, respect for property)
Interior-first specialist for dirty family cars (kids, pets, stains, salt)
Perceived as higher on quality and depth than quick washes or coupon-level details
Good fit for repeat/relationship-oriented customers in east-side suburbs
areas_for_improvement: Not positioned as a long-term protection or rust-prevention specialist
Less suited to fleet and corporate vehicle programs than fleet-focused competitors
Not positioned as a specialist for boats/marinas compared with dedicated marine detailers
Perceived parity rather than clear superiority on convenience and scheduling vs other mobile detailers
Geographic concentration on east-side suburbs limits accessibility for west-side and outlying customers
Limited public review volume compared with large local players makes performance feel less proven at scale
